hot.body: Matt Grossi scored five and assisted on two more in a 9–3 championship-game win. Premier’s whole team scored three. There are difficult individual matchups, and then there is losing the scoring comparison to one bloke.
hot.headline: Grossi: five goals, absolutely no subtlety

hot.body: Eric Mortson and Jeff Lobodzinski each had a goal and four assists in a win. Mortson’s team conceded three; Lobodzinski’s conceded eight. Same output, wildly different amounts of nonsense for the attack to subsidize.
hot.headline: Mortson and Lobodzinski: four helpers apiece

hot.body: Tristan Hatfield’s three goals and two assists ought to make for pleasant reading. Then you get to the 9–8 loss. A hat trick should buy you something better than a front-row seat in the team-defence complaint department.
hot.headline: Hatfield: five points, no team win

cold.body: FitzRays Premier conceded nine in the championship game. Five belonged to Matt Grossi. At some point the word Premier stops being aspirational and becomes evidence. The team defending was bargain-basement stuff at full championship-game prices.
cold.headline: Premier: nine against, branding under review

cold.body: Score eight, lose anyway. FitzRays Flyers found a way to make a hat trick from Tristan Hatfield and two goals from Adrian Hartley insufficient. That attack deserved better than a team-defence bill marked “please send another.”
cold.headline: Flyers: apparently eight was asking too much

cold.body: Kyle Geraghty had three useful assists; Cameron Milne had one. Neither scored in London Eco Metal’s nine-goal win. Nine goals to go around and these two stuck to the side dishes. Productive helpers, yes. Their goal columns still look like they came with the free trial.
cold.headline: Geraghty and Milne: the pass-only club

lead.dek: London Eco Metal wins the championship game 9–3. Matt Grossi scores five; FitzRays Premier makes a compelling case for a name change.
body: London Eco Metal beat FitzRays Premier 9–3 in Thursday, September 24’s championship game, a result that makes “Premier” look less like a team name than a complaint for the advertising regulator. Nine goals against with the championship game on the line. That is a hell of a time to offer wholesale pricing.

Matt Grossi scored five goals and added two assists. Premier managed three goals as an entire team. Grossi beat their collective output himself and still found time to help with somebody else’s. Eric Mortson contributed a goal and four assists to a result Premier will struggle to describe without using the word “shit.”

First General London, meanwhile, beat FitzRays Flyers 9–8 in the third-place game. Tristan Hatfield had a hat trick and five points for the losing side. Apparently eight goals now buys you a valuable lesson about team defence.

Twenty-nine goals across two games gives the first Hockey Life Times plenty to print. The defending gives us considerably less to praise. Eco Metal gets the championship-game win; everyone conceding nine gets the large type.
lead.caption: Matt Grossi, illustrated from his player portrait: five goals and two assists in London Eco Metal’s 9–3 championship-game win.
lead.headline: ECO METAL TURNS PREMIER INTO SCRAP

body: FitzRays Premier lost the championship game 9–3 to London Eco Metal, and there is no respectable way to dress that up. Put a tie on nine goals against and you still have nine goals against. Premier is a lovely name for a team that would prefer you not read the score.

Matt Grossi supplied five goals and two assists. Eric Mortson had a goal and four assists; Cooper Hatfield added a goal and two helpers. Craig Bettridge and Ash Moore also scored. Eco Metal had plenty of contributors, even with Grossi treating the goal column like his personal property.
Dan MacGillivray and Adrian Kwasek scored for Premier, while Jack Foote had an assist. Three goals ought to give a team something to work with. Premier’s defending turned them into a footnote.

Eco Metal earned the championship-game win by six goals. Premier earned a long, uncomfortable look at a result in which one opponent scored more than its entire team. Start the review there. Bring a red pen with a spare cartridge.
games.headline: PREMIER PRICE. CLEARANCE-RACK DEFENCE.

body: First General London beat FitzRays Flyers 9–8 in Thursday’s third-place game. Seventeen goals is a generous serving of hockey and a damning review of the defending. First General gets the win. Anyone proposing a team-defence clinic on the strength of it should have their whiteboard confiscated.

Jeff Lobodzinski had a goal and four assists for First General. Cameron Sheppard scored twice, while Drew Fess, Vince Carducci and Adam Klimowicz each supplied a goal and two assists. That is a lot of useful attacking work to need just to win by one.

Tristan Hatfield scored three goals and added two assists for the Flyers. Adrian Hartley chipped in two goals and an assist. Hatfield produced a hat trick and still belongs in a losing game report, which feels like being charged extra for assembling your own furniture.

The Flyers scored eight. Eight! A team should be embarrassed to make that insufficient. First General can enjoy the third-place win, but conceding eight does rather spoil any attempt to act superior about the defending.
games.headline: EIGHT GOALS SHOULD NOT REQUIRE AN APOLOGY

stars.name: Matt Grossi
stars.reason: EDITORIAL FIRST STAR — Five goals and two assists in the championship-game win. Matt Grossi led the week with seven points and outscored Premier by himself. Usually a team at least makes you bring teammates to that argument.

stars.name: Eric Mortson
stars.reason: EDITORIAL SECOND STAR — A goal and four assists in the 9–3 championship-game win. Eric Mortson supplied enough help to qualify as a public service, provided the public was wearing London Eco Metal colours.

stars.name: Jeff Lobodzinski
stars.reason: EDITORIAL THIRD STAR — A goal and four assists in First General London’s 9–8 third-place win. Jeff Lobodzinski made a substantial contribution to an attack that, regrettably, really did need nine.

aroundRink.body: First General London has three wins and eight points in the current season table. Its 9–8 third-place win does not magically turn that into a glorious campaign, but it is a result worth enjoying. Just keep the celebration speech about the attack. Eight goals against is an awkward number to wave around as proof that the whole operation is fixed.
aroundRink.headline: First General wins something. Let it enjoy it.

aroundRink.body: Cooper Hatfield had a goal and two assists for London Eco Metal; Craig Bettridge added a goal and an assist, and Ash Moore scored once. Grossi gets the enormous headline, but the smaller type matters. Over at First General London, Drew Fess, Vince Carducci and Adam Klimowicz each had a goal and two assists. Plenty of players earned space in this paper without needing the entire front page.
aroundRink.headline: The supporting cast gets some ink

Eco Metal can enjoy the championship-game win while the rest ponder the homework.
